about.title: Manteca Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Manteca sits at the crossroads of SR-120 and SR-99, and roughly 75,000 people here rely on local clinics, urgent care offices, and nearby hospitals for everything from routine checkups to emergency care after a collision on Yosemite Avenue or Main Street. Most of that care goes right. Sometimes it does not, and the difference between an unlucky result and a genuine error can be hard for a patient to see on their own. That is where medical malpractice claims come in. Under California's MICRA framework, a claim generally has to be filed within one year of discovering the harm and never more than three years after the injury itself, with a 90-day notice sent to the provider before any lawsuit. A qualified medical expert almost always has to confirm that the standard of care was breached. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Manteca residents with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Manteca Patients Turn to LawProactive

items.title: MICRA Deadlines Are Short
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from the date you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury, to bring a claim. An attorney can pin down which clock applies to you before it runs out.

items.title: The 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the provider must receive a 90-day pre-suit notice of intent. Getting that step right early keeps your options open.

items.title: Expert Review, Not Guesswork
items.desc: A bad outcome by itself is not malpractice; a qualified medical expert almost always has to confirm the care fell below the accepted standard. The attorneys we connect you with know how to arrange that review.

items.question: I was treated after a crash on SR-120 near Manteca and my injury got worse. Can I have both a car accident claim and a malpractice claim?
items.answer: It is possible. A collision claim addresses the harm caused by the crash itself, while a malpractice claim addresses additional harm caused by negligent care afterward. The two involve different parties, different deadlines, and different proof, so an attorney will usually evaluate them separately. Bring both sets of records to your consultation.

items.question: Does California limit what I can recover in a medical malpractice case?
items.answer: MICRA places a cap on non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, and that cap increases each year under current law. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are handled differently. An attorney can explain how the cap applies to the facts of your situation.
